title: CTPAT Pilot Program Act of 2023
official_summary:
Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism Pilot Program Act of 2023 or the CTPAT Pilot Program Act of 2023

This act requires the Department of Homeland Security to carry out a pilot program that assesses whether allowing certain entities to participate in the Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) would enhance port security, combat terrorism, prevent supply chain security breaches, or otherwise meet the goals of CTPAT.

Such entities are (1) non-asset-based third-party logistics providers that arrange international freight transportation and are licensed by the Department of Transportation; or (2) asset-based third-party logistics providers that facilitate cross-border activity, are licensed or bonded by specified federal agencies, and execute logistics services using their own warehousing assets and resources.

The act requires the Government Accountability Office to report on the effectiveness of CTPAT.

summary.headline: New law requires a pilot program testing whether certain freight logistics companies should be allowed to join a federal supply chain security partnership.
summary.what_it_does: The Department of Homeland Security must run a pilot program that lets certain third-party logistics companies take part in the Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT). CTPAT is a voluntary program where businesses work with the government on cargo and supply chain security. The pilot will test whether including these companies improves port security, helps fight terrorism, or prevents supply chain security breaches. The Government Accountability Office must also report on how well CTPAT works.

who_it_affects.how: Companies licensed by the Department of Transportation that arrange international freight shipping, without owning the equipment themselves, may be able to join CTPAT through the pilot.
Companies that handle cross-border shipping using their own warehouses and resources, and are licensed or bonded by certain federal agencies, may be able to join CTPAT through the pilot.
The department must set up and run the pilot program to judge whether adding these companies meets CTPAT's security goals.
The office must study and report on how effective CTPAT is.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 1, 2024; the summary does not give specific start dates or deadlines for the pilot or report.
